tagline: Down the old bay-side roads of the upper Eastern Shore.
intro: The byway starts at Chesapeake City, where the C&D Canal cuts the town in two, and heads south on MD 213 across the Sassafras River to Chestertown, then by way of Centreville and Queenstown onto Kent Island and Stevensville, by the Bay Bridge. A spur runs out on MD 20 to Rock Hall and the Eastern Neck refuge. These are the old main roads, bypassed since by US 50 and US 301, through farmland and towns kept from the 18th and 19th centuries.
The state carries the route on south to Crisfield, 419 miles in all, where the downtown is said to stand on oyster shells and the boats leave for Smith Island.

moments.title: Chesapeake City
moments.text: A freighter took out the canal drawbridge in 1942. The new bridge had to clear supertankers, and stood so high that traffic crossing the canal stopped coming through town.

moments.title: Chestertown
moments.text: A colonial port at the head of the Chester River, second only to Annapolis for 18th-century houses, and in 1790 the center of the nation's population.

moments.title: Rock Hall
moments.text: Named for a mansion of white sandstone. Its railroad never came, the company going bankrupt in 1877, and the harbor still keeps a fleet of commercial watermen.
